cards.text: The tabernacle is finally up, and the glory of the LORD has filled it (Exodus 40:34). Now the LORD calls to Moses, Israel's leader, and speaks to him from the Tent of Meeting. He gives Moses a message for the Israelites about bringing offerings to Him.

cards.question: In His message for the Israelites, the LORD says only the priests may bring Him an offering.

cards.text: First up, the burnt offering. If it's from the herd, God says the man is to present an unblemished male and bring it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

cards.question: Why does the man bring his burnt offering to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting?

answers.text: So the LORD will accept it
So the elders can inspect it
So the people can watch it

cards.text: He can't just drop it off like a cookie box on a porch and run. He walks up and lays his hand on the animal's head.

cards.question: The man lays his hand on the head of his burnt offering. What does the LORD say that's for?

answers.text: So it can make atonement for him
So the priest knows it is his
So it stays calm at the altar

cards.text: He slaughters the young bull before the LORD, and Aaron's sons, the priests, splatter its blood on all sides of the altar. That's Aaron, Moses's brother. The man skins it and cuts it into pieces, and the priests arrange the pieces on the burning wood, head and fat included. The entrails and legs are washed with water, and the priest burns all of it on the altar.

cards.question: The LORD calls the burnt offering, burned on the altar, a pleasing aroma to Him.

cards.text: If the burnt offering is from the flock, sheep or goats, God says it's an unblemished male too. It's slaughtered on the north side of the altar, and then it goes much like the bull: blood on the altar, pieces on the fire, entrails and legs washed, and all of it burned.

And if the burnt offering is birds, God says it's a turtledove or a young pigeon. The priest twists off its head at the altar, drains its blood on the side and throws the crop to the east side, in the place for ashes. Then he tears it open by its wings, without dividing it completely, and burns it on the altar. It's a pleasing aroma to the LORD too.

Now the LORD moves from animals to grain, and friend, I'm a cookie stamper, so this is my DEPARTMENT. When anyone brings a grain offering, it's fine flour with olive oil and frankincense on it, and the priest burns a handful, with all the frankincense, on the altar as a memorial portion.

cards.question: The priest burns a handful of a grain offering as a memorial portion. Who gets the rest of it?

cards.text: Then the LORD covers grain offerings baked in an oven, made on a griddle or cooked in a pan, all made of fine flour with oil. He said OVEN, friend. Now we're talking MY language. Any way it's made, it goes to the priest, who burns the memorial portion on the altar.

cards.question: Then the LORD draws a line: no grain offering presented to Him may be made with ___.

cards.text: And not honey either. The LORD says no leaven or honey is to be burned as a food offering to Him.

cards.question: Leaven and honey can't be brought to the LORD in any offering at all.

cards.text: Then the LORD says to season every grain offering with salt, and leaving it out is NOT an option.

cards.question: What does the LORD call the salt that goes in every grain offering?

answers.text: The salt of the covenant of your God
The salt of the altar of your God
The salt of the house of your God

cards.text: Last, if someone brings a grain offering of firstfruits, it's crushed heads of new grain roasted on the fire, with oil and frankincense on it. The priest burns the memorial portion of it, with all its frankincense, as a food offering to the LORD.

Now a new one: the peace offering. If it's from the herd, God says it can be male or female, without blemish, and the man lays his hand on its head and slaughters it at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. The priests splatter the blood on all sides of the altar, then burn the fat covering the entrails, both kidneys with their fat and the lobe of the liver on top of the burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

A lamb from the flock goes the same way: male or female without blemish, hand on the head, blood on the altar. A lamb adds the entire fat tail to the list, and the priest burns it all on the altar as a food offering to the LORD.
A goat goes the same way too: hand on its head, blood on the altar, and the same fat, kidneys and liver lobe come off for the LORD.

cards.question: After the priest burns the goat's portion as a pleasing aroma, the LORD says: All the ___ is the LORD's.

cards.text: Then the LORD closes with one more rule for the Israelites, about what they must not eat. Lean in, friend, this is the kind of rule you tape to the fridge.

cards.question: In the LORD's closing rule, the Israelites must not eat any fat or any what?
The LORD says the rule about fat and blood only lasts while Israel is camped around the tabernacle.

cards.text: A permanent statute for the generations to come, wherever they live, which beats the expired coupon I shared a junk drawer with by a LOT. And the LORD isn't done teaching about offerings yet, friend, so keep that apron on.
